lines: Walls help, but walls do not swing back. You did.
A village stands on more than stone. Yesterday, it stood on nerve.
The wall held better because someone stood beyond it.
You gave the village another layer of stone when it needed one.
I saw <red><bold>raiders</bold></red> hit our edge and fail to break through.
Good work under pressure keeps structures standing. So does courage.
The village is still square on its foundation because people held firm.
You helped keep the center from cracking.
You stood where the stonework broke and gave the village a new line.
The golem was not the only one protecting us that day.
You kept your head when the square filled with smoke and arrows.
Those walls can be rebuilt because people survived behind them.
I saw you return for someone who could not run.
The raiders expected a weak edge. You made them pay for that guess.
Your warning reached the far houses before the first crossbow bolt did.
You did not chase glory. You stayed where we needed you.
The repairs show how hard the attack was. The head count shows what you saved.
I will remember who carried stone and who carried neighbors.
The village owes you more than cheers by the well.
If the horn sounds again, I hope you are standing with us.
